newsitem.title: JAPAN: JSDA investigating deals in Olympic Sports.
newsitem.headline: JSDA investigating deals in Olympic Sports.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) said on Wednesday that it was investigating buy and sell orders for Olympic Sports Co shares to check some transactions which took place before the company's shares were taken off the over-the-counter (OTC) market last week.

JSDA Vice Chairman Kaname Seki told a regular news conference that while Olympic Sports had filed for court mediation with creditors on September 17, it did not reveal the fact to its lead manager and the JSDA until late on September 19.
Daily volume in Olympic Sports' shares rose in the three days before September 20, when the JSDA suspended trade in the sports equipment retailer, industry sources said.

Under JSDA rules, issuers must inform lead managers of important issues which would affect investors' judgement, Seki said. Olympic Sports shares are now traded as monitored stocks, which are traded for up to six months after the registration cancellation.
On Wednesday, the shares were ask-only at 311 yen. Since the shares closed on September 19 at 471 yen, no actual transactions have taken place, Seki said.
